entries.command:
cd . && gh pr create --base master --head feat/commit-ledger --title "feat(ledger): agent history per commit, on an agent-ledger branch" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Shows what the agent did for each commit of a range, e.g. this PR's `master..feat/commit-ledger`.

## How it works
- `vp run ledger -- sync [--range main..HEAD] [--no-outputs]` finds the session that made each commit and writes the history slice to a separate `agent-ledger` branch: `commits/<sha>.json` + `patch-ids.json`. It uses git plumbing only, so HEAD and the working tree are never touched. Share the ledger with `git push origin agent-ledger`.
- Matching: a SHA printed by `git commit` wins; otherwise the latest `git commit` (in command position) up to 10 min before the commit time. A command that makes several commits matches each of them.
- Segment: from the thread's previous commit action up to this one. Leading discussion-only turns are dropped, and the prompt is kept when a segment starts mid-turn.
- After a rebase or amend, `git patch-id --stable` finds the entry again.
- Outputs are redacted like proof-of-work exports.
- Viewer: `#/ledger?repo=<path>&range=<range>` lists commits, each with the turn → phase → action tree (read-only `ActionView`).

## Try it on this PR
The `agent-ledger` branch is pushed and has entries for all 7 commits here.
```
git fetch origin agent-ledger:agent-ledger
#/ledger?repo=<your clone>&range=master..feat/commit-ledger
```

## Not included
- No post-commit hook: sync is manual.
- Claude Code sessions outside T3 are not read.

## Tests
`vp test run` (79), `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`. Ledger tests run against a real temp git repo: time/sha matching, redaction, an untouched worktree, idempotent re-sync, and patch-id lookup after an amend.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://<url>)
EOF
)"

entries.text: The issue is CI lacks a git identity, so the service's git calls during ledger.sync fail. I should fix this in the test by setting repo-local user.name/email config after init, since real users would already have their identity configured.
CI has no git identity, so `commit-tree` fails inside the test repo. I'll set a repo-local identity in the test.

entries.command:
cd . && python3 - <<'EOF'
p="src/server/Ledger.test.ts"; s=open(p).read()
a='''        yield* git(repo, ["init", "-q", "-b", "main"]);
'''
assert a in s
s=s.replace(a,a+'''        // The service's own git calls (commit-tree) need an identity; CI has none globally.
        yield* git(repo, ["config", "user.name", "Agent"]);
        yield* git(repo, ["config", "user.email", "agent@example.test"]);
''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
